reviewer_corrections: Initial script/report retained with -initial: reviewer incorrectly expected an etc/client-pin.txt entry in executable/module-only payload provenance. Corrected to a source-derived pin construction check; actual pin file bytes are not claimed. Original run bytes unchanged.
limits: TLS1.3 ServerHello version and ClientHello ALPN offer/SNI are plaintext observations. Encrypted ALPN selection, peer Certificate/CertificateVerify and TLS payload are not decrypted or independently proven by PCAP.
Public DER chain/EKU/SAN/guest-time validation is offline fixture validation, linked by audited payload/TLS/loader source; it is not extraction of the encrypted certificate handshake.

Actual /etc TLS JSON files, client-pin.txt bytes and key/config mode snapshots were not collected. Root manifest, helper policy, root resource receipts, executed init generation logic, public DER and live TLS streams are checked; actual TLS JSON/pin bytes/modes are not claimed.
The test grants its client principal both devices. It does not test a valid but ungranted remote certificate or arbitrary local/root bypass.
Absence of specified clear signatures/recognizable URB headers is bounded to these entire captured links, not a universal proof of no information leakage.
Metrics are successful application reads/writes including headers/partial writes, not USB payload/TLS bytes, throughput, RTT or heartbeat.
Killed serial-session counters are only last persisted samples; no fabricated final counters/old terminal0. Round2 closes the tty FD before KILL, so no particular USB URB/ioctl pending-at-KILL proof.
Minimal bounded field/known-fixture/DER/PEM scan of app state/audit cannot prove absence of every imaginable secret; raw USB test artifacts intentionally exist separately.
No real hardware G1/G2, ISO, crash FD revocation, or full Phase3 completion claim.
